dod_intent_evidence: Own Series A announcement states "we were able to close over $7M in contracts in a span of just 60 days across the US Department of Defense"; AFRL SBIR contract on usaspending in news section.
score_evidence: "Deploy Everywhere / Detect Everything ... Hot-Swappable Commercial Components ... AI-Enabled Workflows For Experts" — homepage is capability-brag headers with no operational constraints stated → lab_language_intensity

Series A letter is operationally fluent ("Soldiers on the front lines are forced to use hobbyist lab equipment ... We cannot place large numbers of million-dollar sensors across the ocean and constantly deploy experts to operate them") — keeps deployment/operator subscores low
Open role "Mission Operations Engineer" is a field-facing hire → hiring_profile_skew low

blind_spots.blind_spot: "Hot-Swappable Commercial Components" — COTS RF hardware chosen for cost has never seen salt fog, dust, 50°C heat, or gloved-hand swaps at an austere Pacific site; component hot-swap assumes a bench, not a berm.
blind_spots.operator_reality: The E-5 maintaining a mesh node OCONUS has no spares pipeline for consumer SDR components and no RF expert on site; a dead $100 component with no MIL-spec substitute takes the node off the mesh until resupply.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their disruption thesis is cost ('bridges the gap between $100 off-the-shelf hardware and the existing $1M+ systems') — ruggedization and sustainment logistics cut directly against that pitch.

blind_spots.blind_spot: "Unlimited Downstream Integrations" collides with the accreditation boundary: every DoD network their sensor data touches needs an ATO, and EW sensor data feeds (SIGINT-adjacent) carry classification and ITAR handling their public language never mentions.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A vast detection mesh whose data can't cross into the mission network inside the funded period is a science project; integration in DoD means IL levels, cross-domain solutions, and prime/GFE backends, not APIs.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team is Raytheon/Lockheed engineering plus Google/Microsoft software pedigree; the compliance-side words (ATO, RMF, ITAR, CMMC) appear nowhere in ~1,400 words of their own language.

blind_spots.blind_spot: "AI-Enabled Workflows For Experts" targets experts while their own Series A letter argues legacy systems fail because they 'require co-located, trained experts' — the actual fielded user is a minimally-trained operator, and the training/sustainment chain for thousands of distributed nodes is unaddressed.
blind_spots.operator_reality: At scale across the Pacific there is no expert per node; whoever is on site gets 20 minutes of training, and the workflow either survives that or the mesh degrades silently.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Early contracts likely put their own engineers next to the sensor; the expert-in-the-loop assumption hasn't been stress-tested by a deployment they didn't attend.

opener_hook: Distributed Spectrum's Series A letter says the US can't scatter million-dollar sensors and experts across the Pacific — yet every network a cheap mesh node's data touches still needs an ATO the funded clock rarely survives.
what_they_do: Builds low-cost AI-enabled RF sensors and software that detect and identify radio signals for electronic warfare and spectrum awareness.
